line: No Limit, I never care
vault_lines: No Limit, I never care
meaning:
The No Limit Muskegon Boys (NLMB) is a gang based on the East Side of Chicago, Illinois which built a name due to its inclusion of G Herbo and Lil Bibby, the rapper-turned-manager who rose to fame alongside Herb in the early 2010s. While NLMB is generally thought of as a street gang, Herb views the group in a bit of a different light:

It’s a brotherhood. It ain’t no clique, no gang, or nothing like that. […] I don’t be on the South Side or West Side, we straight East Side. I’m known on the East Side. […] We not associated with no [Gangster Disciples], Vice Lords, or none of that.

The latter half of the line is a possible call back to Herb’s December 2017 track “Never Cared,” where he outlines his gang activity and shouts out NLMB’s home block, Essex. The track saw commercial success thanks in large part to Durk’s viral September 2018 remix of it, “No Auto Durk,” and it also received a remake from Chicago rapper Polo G.

The phrase is also reminiscent of Herb and fellow NLMB affiliate Juice WRLD’s February 2019 collaboration, “Never Scared,” as the two repeatedly rap it in the chorus.

meaning:
Lil Durk alludes to his feature on Pooh Shiesty’s November 2020 hit single, “Back in Blood,” from the latter’s debut mixtape, Shiesty Season (2021). To get something “back in blood” means to seek revenge through violence.

Here, Durk uses the song and phrase to describe his involvement in gang activity, indicating that he successfully got payback for a wrong done against him without alerting the public or the authorities. He also shows his appreciation for the song’s success and his collaborator, who was incarcerated due to gun charges at the time of this song’s release.
